skill.name: documentation-writer
skill.description: Guides the assistant to plan and write Diataxis-based software documentation, including tutorials, how-to guides, reference pages, and explanations.
skill.summary: Creates Diataxis-based software documentation with clear scope, audience, outlines, and Markdown drafts.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: Reviewed the prompt-only SKILL.md and found no confirmed security issues. The only static finding is a public Diataxis reference URL, which does not create a network operation, exfiltration path, or prompt injection concern.

static_findings.snippet: Your work is strictly guided by the principles and structure of the Diátaxis Framework (https://diat

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 9 references the public Diataxis Framework URL as documentation context. The skill is prompt-only and contains no instruction or code that performs a network request.

content.value_statement: Teams often need documentation that matches user intent across tutorials, how-to guides, reference pages, and explanations. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to clarify scope, propose an outline, and draft structured Markdown.
actual_capabilities: Classifies documentation as tutorials, how-to guides, reference pages, or explanations.
Asks clarifying questions about document type, audience, user goal, and scope.
Proposes a detailed outline before drafting the full document.
Writes well-formatted Markdown after the outline is approved.
Uses provided Markdown files for tone and terminology without copying unless asked.
Avoids external sources unless the user provides a link and gives explicit instruction.
limitations: It is prompt guidance only and does not include scripts or automation.
It needs product details to avoid generic or inaccurate documentation.
It waits for outline approval before writing the full draft.
It does not verify current technical facts without approved sources.

use_cases.title: Plan Product Tutorials
use_cases.description: Create a learning-focused outline and draft for users who need a guided first success.

use_cases.title: Write Operational How-To Guides
use_cases.description: Turn a specific task into a clear sequence of steps with scope and prerequisites.

use_cases.title: Draft Reference Pages
use_cases.description: Organize technical facts into concise reference material for repeat lookup and maintenance.

prompt_templates.title: Classify My Documentation Request
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for choosing the right documentation type.
prompt_templates.prompt: I need documentation for [product or feature]. Help me choose whether it should be a tutorial, how-to guide, reference page, or explanation. Ask any clarifying questions first.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Diataxis Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for structure before drafting.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Diataxis-based outline for a [document type] about [topic]. The target audience is [audience], the goal is [goal], and the scope is [scope].

prompt_templates.title: Draft the Approved Document
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request after approving an outline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the approved outline to write the full Markdown document. Keep the language simple, accurate, and consistent with the provided product details.

prompt_templates.title: Align a Documentation Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for improving multiple related documents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these documentation drafts for Diataxis alignment. Identify mixed purposes, missing audience context, scope problems, and terminology inconsistencies before proposing revisions.

output_examples.input: A request to write onboarding documentation for a new developer feature.
output_examples.output: Clarifying questions about audience and goal, followed by a tutorial outline focused on a first successful outcome.

output_examples.input: An approved outline for a deployment task.
output_examples.output: A Markdown how-to guide with prerequisites, ordered steps, expected results, and concise troubleshooting notes.

output_examples.input: Existing Markdown files that define the product tone and terminology.
output_examples.output: A revised documentation draft that follows the same voice, naming, and structure without copying source text.

best_practices: Provide the target audience, user goal, scope, and document type at the start.
Review and approve the proposed outline before requesting the final draft.
Share existing documentation when tone, terminology, or structure must match.
anti_patterns: Requesting a full document without product details or a clear user goal.
Mixing tutorial, reference, and explanation goals in one page.
Asking for external research without providing trusted links or instructions.

faq.question: What documentation framework does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the Diataxis framework, which separates tutorials, how-to guides, reference pages, and explanations.

faq.question: Does it write the final document immediately?
faq.answer: No. It first asks clarifying questions and proposes an outline before writing the full Markdown draft.

faq.question: Can it match our existing documentation style?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide Markdown examples, and it can use them for tone, terminology, and structure.

faq.question: Can it use external websites as sources?
faq.answer: Only when you provide a link and explicitly instruct it to use that source.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this skill safe to install?
faq.answer: It is a prompt-only skill with no scripts. The audit found no confirmed security issue.
